Ch. 4 // Talk Ten // USC Gould School of Law Commencement Address
The University of Southern California

USC Gould School of Law Commencement Address南加州大学古尔德法学院毕业致辞

No doubt many of you are wondering why this speaker is so old. Well, the answer is obvious: He hasn’t died yet. And why was this speaker chosen? Well, I don’t know that. I’d like to think that the development department had nothing to do with it.

你们当中想必有许多人都在纳闷，为什么这位演讲者如此年迈。好吧，答案显而易见：他还没死呢。那么，又为什么要选这位演讲者呢？这个我也不知道。我倒愿意相信，这事跟学校的拓展募捐部门毫无关系。

Whatever the reason, I think it’s fitting that I’m speaking here because I see a crowd of older people in the rear, not wearing robes. And I know, from having educated an army of descendants, who it is that really deserves a lot of the honors that are being given today to the robe-wearing students in front. The sacrifices and the wisdom and the value transfer that come from one generation to the next should always be appreciated.

不管出于什么原因，我觉得自己来这里演讲是恰如其分的，因为我看到后排坐了一群年纪较长、没有穿学位袍的人。我自己培养了一大群子孙，所以我深知，今天坐在前面、身披学位袍的学子们，他们所获得的诸多荣誉，真正当之无愧的其实是后面那些人。一代人向下一代人所作的牺牲、所传授的智慧与价值观，理应永远受到感念。

I also take pleasure from the sea of Asian faces to my left. All my life I have admired Confucius. I like the idea of filial piety,394Filial pietyIn Confucian thought, filial piety —a love and respect for one’s parents and ancestors—is a virtue to be cultivated. More broadly, filial piety means to take care of one’s parents; not be rebellious; show love, respect, and support; display courtesy; ensure male heirs; uphold fraternity among brothers; wisely advise one’s parents; conceal their mistakes; display sorrow for their sickness and death; and carry out sacrifices after their death. Confucius (551–479 BC) believed that if people could learn to fulfill their filial roles properly, they would be better able to perform their roles in society and government. To Confucius, filial piety was so essential he felt it transcended the law. In fact, during parts of the Han Dynasty, those who neglected ancestor worship according to filial piety precepts were subject to corporal punishment.在儒家思想中，孝（filial piety）——对父母和祖先的爱与尊敬——是一种需要培养的美德。更广义地说，孝意味着照顾父母；不叛逆；表达爱、尊敬和支持；讲究礼貌；确保男性继承人；在兄弟间维护友爱；明智地劝谏父母；掩饰他们的过错；为他们的疾病和去世表达哀痛；并在他们身后举行祭祀。孔子（公元前 551–前 479 年）认为，如果人们能学会恰当履行自己的孝道角色，就能更好地在社会和政府中扮演自己的角色。对孔子而言，孝至关重要，他认为孝超越法律。事实上，在汉代的部分时期，那些不按孝道规诫祭祖的人会受到体罚。 of ideas or values that are taught and duties that come naturally that should be passed onto the next generation. You people who don’t think there’s anything in this idea, please note how fast Asian people are rising in American life. I think they have something.

我还很高兴地看到，我的左侧是一片亚洲人的面孔之海。我这一生始终敬仰孔子393Confucius孔子（Confucius）。我欣赏“孝道”的理念——那些应当被教导的思想与价值观，以及天然就应承担的责任，都应当代代相传。

All right, I’ve scratched out a few notes, and I’m going to try and give an account of certain ideas and attitudes that have worked well for me. I don’t claim that they’re perfect for everybody. But I think many of them contain universal values and that many of them are can’t-fail ideas.

好吧，我已经草草记下几点提纲，接下来我想试着讲述一些对我颇有裨益的思想与态度。我不敢说它们对每个人都完美无缺，但我认为其中许多蕴含着普世价值，而且有许多是“屡试不爽”的道理。

What are the core ideas that helped me? Well, luckily I had the idea at a very early age that the safest way to try to get what you want is to try to deserve what you want. It’s such a simple idea. It’s the golden rule. You want to deliver to the world what you would buy if you were on the other end. There is no ethos in my opinion that is better for any lawyer or any other person to have. By and large, the people who have had this ethos win in life, and they don’t win just money and honors. They win the respect, the deserved trust of the people they deal with. And there is huge pleasure in life to be obtained from getting deserved trust.

那么，是哪些核心思想帮了我呢？说来幸运，我在很小的时候就明白了一个道理：要想得到自己想要的东西，最稳妥的办法，是让自己配得上它。这是再简单不过的道理，也就是黄金法则。你应当交付给这个世界的，正是倘若你处在另一端、你愿意买单的东西。在我看来，无论对律师还是对任何其他人，没有哪种精神比这更可宝贵。大体而言，秉持这种精神的人会在人生中获胜，而且他们赢得的绝不只是金钱与荣誉。他们赢得的是尊重，是与之打交道的人理所应当给予他们的信任。而获得这份应得的信任，正是人生中莫大的乐事。

你应当交付给这个世界的，正是倘若你处在另一端、你愿意买单的东西。

“You want to deliver to the world what you would buy if you were on the other end.”你想交付给世界的，应是若你站在另一端、自己也愿意买下的东西。

Now, occasionally you will find a perfect rogue of a person who dies rich and widely known. But mostly these people are fully understood as despicable by the surrounding civilization. If the cathedral is full of people at the funeral ceremony, most of them are there to celebrate the fact that the person is dead.

当然，偶尔你也会发现某个彻头彻尾的无赖，死时既富有又声名远播。但多数情况下，周遭的文明早已将此类人视作可鄙之徒。倘若葬礼上教堂里挤满了人，那么其中大多数人其实是为庆祝此人终于离世而来。

That reminds me of the story of the time when one of these people died, and the minister said, “It’s now time to say something nice about the deceased.”395Say something nice about the deceased说点逝者的好话 And nobody came forward, and nobody came forward, and nobody came forward. And finally, one man came up and said, “Well, his brother was worse.” That is not where you want to go. A life ending in such a funeral is not the life you want to have.

这让我想起一个故事：这类人当中有一位离世，牧师说：“现在是时候对逝者说点好话了。”可没人站出来，没人站出来，还是没人站出来。终于，有个人走上前来说：“呃，他弟弟比他还糟。”那可不是你想落得的境地。以这样一场葬礼收尾的人生，绝非你想要的那种人生。

The second idea that I developed very early is that there’s no love that’s so right as admiration-based love, and such love should include the instructive dead. Somehow I picked up that idea, and I’ve lived with it all my life. It’s been very useful to me. A love like that described by [William] Somerset Maugham in his book Of Human Bondage396Of Human BondageOf Human Bondage , William Somerset Maugham’s autobiographical 1915 novel, is generally considered his masterpiece. The protagonist, Philip, meets Mildred, a London waitress, who snubs him. Falling in obsessive love with Mildred, Philip knows he is foolish and despises himself. He gives Mildred all his money; she repays him with disgust and humiliation. As Maugham describes the relationship: “Love was like a parasite in his legs nourishing a hateful existence on his life’s blood; it absorbed his existence so intensely that he could take pleasure in nothing else.”《人性的枷锁》（Of Human Bondage）是威廉·萨默塞特·毛姆（William Somerset Maugham）1915 年的自传体小说，generally 被认为是他的代表作。主人公菲利普遇到了伦敦女侍者米尔德里德，后者冷落了他。菲利普疯狂地爱上了米尔德里德，明知自己愚蠢而自我鄙视。他把所有的钱都给了米尔德里德；她回报他的却是厌恶和羞辱。正如毛姆对这段关系的描述：“爱就像他腿里的一条寄生虫，靠他生命之血滋养着一种可憎的存在；它如此强烈地吞噬了他的存在，以至于他无法从任何别的事情中获得快乐。” is a sick kind of love. It’s a disease, and if you find yourself with a disease like that, you should eliminate it.

我很小就形成的第二个想法是：没有哪种爱，比以仰慕为基础的爱情更正恰当；而这种爱，理应将那些能给人以教益的逝者也包括在内。不知怎的，我汲取了这个想法，并一生奉行。它对我裨益良多。萨默塞特·毛姆（Somerset Maugham）在其著作《人性的枷锁396Of Human BondageOf Human Bondage , William Somerset Maugham’s autobiographical 1915 novel, is generally considered his masterpiece. The protagonist, Philip, meets Mildred, a London waitress, who snubs him. Falling in obsessive love with Mildred, Philip knows he is foolish and despises himself. He gives Mildred all his money; she repays him with disgust and humiliation. As Maugham describes the relationship: “Love was like a parasite in his legs nourishing a hateful existence on his life’s blood; it absorbed his existence so intensely that he could take pleasure in nothing else.”《人性的枷锁》（Of Human Bondage）是威廉·萨默塞特·毛姆（William Somerset Maugham）1915 年的自传体小说，generally 被认为是他的代表作。主人公菲利普遇到了伦敦女侍者米尔德里德，后者冷落了他。菲利普疯狂地爱上了米尔德里德，明知自己愚蠢而自我鄙视。他把所有的钱都给了米尔德里德；她回报他的却是厌恶和羞辱。正如毛姆对这段关系的描述：“爱就像他腿里的一条寄生虫，靠他生命之血滋养着一种可憎的存在；它如此强烈地吞噬了他的存在，以至于他无法从任何别的事情中获得快乐。”》（Of Human Bondage）中所描写的那种爱，是一种病态的爱。那是一种疾病，而如果你发现自己染上了这样的病，就应当把它治好。

Another idea—and this may remind you of Confucius, too—is that the acquisition of wisdom is a moral duty. It’s not something you do just to advance in life. And there’s a corollary to that idea that is very important. It requires that you’re hooked on lifetime learning. Without lifetime learning, you people are not going to do very well. You are not going to get very far in life based on what you already know. You’re going to advance in life by what you learn after you leave here.

另一个想法——这或许也会让你们想起孔子（Confucius）——是：获取智慧是一种道德责任。你追求智慧，不只是为了在生活中更上层楼。而这个想法有一个极其重要的推论，那就是：你必须迷上终身学习。没有终身学习，你们这些人不会有多大出息。仅凭已有的知识，你们在人生中走不了多远。你们离开这里之后的所学，才将推动你们向前。

获取智慧是一种道德责任。

“The acquisition of wisdom is a moral duty.”获取智慧，是一项道德义务。

Consider Berkshire Hathaway, one of the best-regarded corporations in the world. It may have the best long-term, big-assets-involving investment record in the history of civilization. The skill that got Berkshire through one decade would not have sufficed to get it through the next decade with comparable levels of achievement. Warren Buffett had to be a continuous learning machine.

且看伯克希尔·哈撒韦（Berkshire Hathaway），它是全球最受敬重的公司之一。它或许拥有人类文明史上最出色、涉及大额资产的长期投资纪录。让伯克希尔（Berkshire Hathaway）熬过一个十年的本事，不足以让它以同等水准再熬过下一个十年。沃伦·巴菲特280Warren Buffett沃伦·巴菲特（Warren Buffett）不得不成为一台持续学习的机器。

The same requirement exists in lower walks of life. I constantly see people rise in life who are not the smartest, sometimes not even the most diligent. But they are learning machines. They go to bed every night a little wiser than they were that morning. And boy, does that habit help, particularly when you have a long run ahead of you.

较低层面的生活，同样有此要求。我不断看到这样一些人，他们在人生中步步高升，却并非最聪明，有时甚至不是最勤奋。但他们是学习机器。他们每天夜里上床时，都比当天早晨聪明了一点点。天哪，这个习惯多有用啊，尤其当你前面还有漫漫长路的时候。

Alfred North Whitehead397Alfred North WhiteheadAlfred North Whitehead (1861–1947) , a British philosopher and mathematician, worked in logic, mathematics, philosophy of science, and metaphysics. Whitehead is known for developing process philosophy, a view holding that fundamental elements of the universe are occasions of experience. In this view, concrete objects are actually successions of these occasions of experience. By grouping occasions of experience, something as complex as a human being can be defined. Whitehead’s views evolved into process theology, a way of understanding God. His best-known mathematics work is Principia Mathematica , co-written with Bertrand Russell.阿尔弗雷德·诺斯·怀特海（Alfred North Whitehead，1861–1947 年）是英国哲学家和数学家，研究逻辑、数学、科学哲学和形而上学。怀特海以发展过程哲学闻名，该观点认为宇宙的基本元素是“经验的机缘”。依此观点，具体的对象实际上是这些经验机缘的延续。通过对经验机缘加以分组，诸如人类这样复杂的事物也能得到定义。怀特海的观点后来演化为过程神学，一种理解上帝的方式。他最著名的数学著作是与伯特兰·罗素（Bertrand Russell）合著的《数学原理》（Principia Mathematica）。 correctly said at one time that the rapid advance of civilization came only when man “invented the method of invention.”398Invent the method of invention发明发明的方法 He was referring to the huge growth in GDP per capita and many other good things we now take for granted. Big-time progress started a few hundred years ago. Before that, progress per century was almost nil. Just as civilization can progress only when it invents the method of invention, you can progress only when you learn the method of learning.

阿尔弗雷德·诺斯·怀特海397Alfred North WhiteheadAlfred North Whitehead (1861–1947) , a British philosopher and mathematician, worked in logic, mathematics, philosophy of science, and metaphysics. Whitehead is known for developing process philosophy, a view holding that fundamental elements of the universe are occasions of experience. In this view, concrete objects are actually successions of these occasions of experience. By grouping occasions of experience, something as complex as a human being can be defined. Whitehead’s views evolved into process theology, a way of understanding God. His best-known mathematics work is Principia Mathematica , co-written with Bertrand Russell.阿尔弗雷德·诺斯·怀特海（Alfred North Whitehead，1861–1947 年）是英国哲学家和数学家，研究逻辑、数学、科学哲学和形而上学。怀特海以发展过程哲学闻名，该观点认为宇宙的基本元素是“经验的机缘”。依此观点，具体的对象实际上是这些经验机缘的延续。通过对经验机缘加以分组，诸如人类这样复杂的事物也能得到定义。怀特海的观点后来演化为过程神学，一种理解上帝的方式。他最著名的数学著作是与伯特兰·罗素（Bertrand Russell）合著的《数学原理》（Principia Mathematica）。（Alfred North Whitehead）曾正确地指出：人类文明的迅猛进步，只有当人类“发明了发明的方法”之后才会出现。他指的是人均GDP的巨幅增长，以及如今我们视为理所当然的许多其他好事。真正意义上的大步前进，始于几百年前。在那之前，每个世纪的进步几乎为零。正如文明唯有发明了发明的方法才能进步，你们也只有学会了学习的方法才能进步。

正如文明唯有发明了发明的方法才能进步，你们也只有学会了学习的方法才能进步。

fig 399
—
Bertrand Russell, coauthor with Alfred North Whitehead of Principia Mathematica
“Just as civilization can progress only when it invents the method of invention, you can progress only when you learn the method of learning.”正如文明只有发明了『发明的方法』才能进步，你也只有学会了『学习的方法』才能进步。

I was very lucky. I came to law school having learned the method of learning, and nothing has served me better in my long life than continuous learning. Consider Warren Buffett again. If you watched him with a time clock, you’d find that about half of his waking time is spent reading. Then a big chunk of the rest of his time is spent talking one-on-one, either on the telephone or personally, with highly gifted people whom he trusts and who trust him. Viewed up close, Warren looks quite academic as he achieves worldly success.

我非常幸运。我在进法学院之前就已经学会了学习的方法，而在这漫长的一生中，没有什么比持续学习对我更有用了。再来看看沃伦·巴菲特400Warren Buffett沃伦·巴菲特（Warren Buffett）。倘若你拿计时器观察他，会发现他清醒时大约一半的时间花在阅读上。剩余时间里很大一块，则用来与一些才华横溢、他信任且也信任他的人一对一交谈——要么打电话，要么面谈。就近观察，沃伦在取得世俗成功的同时，看起来倒颇有几分学究气。

Academia has many wonderful values in it. I came across an example not too long ago. In my capacity as a hospital board chairman, I was dealing with a medical school academic named Joseph M. Mirra, MD.401Joseph M. Mirra, MDJoseph M. Mirra , MD, is a bone and soft tissue pathologist in the Department of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center in Los Angeles. Dr. Mirra’s research interest is bone pathology, about which he has published more than 150 papers, produced 16 book chapters, and edited two books. Board-certified in anatomic and clinical pathology, Dr. Mirra is a sought-after visiting professor who also speaks nationally and internationally on bone pathology. He has been active in medical student teaching throughout his career and has participated in several symposia on bone tumor pathology.约瑟夫·M·米拉（Joseph M. Mirra）医学博士，是洛杉矶西达斯-西奈医学中心（Cedars-Sinai Medical Center）病理学与检验医学系的一位骨与软组织病理学家。米拉博士的研究兴趣是骨病理学，他已就此发表 150 多篇论文，撰写了 16 个图书章节，并编辑了两部著作。米拉博士拥有解剖病理学和临床病理学的专科认证，是一位备受欢迎的客座教授，还在国内外就骨病理学发表演讲。他整个职业生涯都积极参与医学生教学，并参加过多次骨肿瘤病理学专题讨论会。 This man, over years of disciplined work, made himself know more about bone tumor pathology than almost anyone else in the world. He wanted to pass this knowledge on to help treat bone cancer. How was he going to do it? Well, he decided to write a textbook, and even though I don’t think a textbook like this sells more than a few thousand copies, they do end up in cancer treatment centers all over the world. He took a sabbatical year and sat down at his computer with all his slides, carefully saved and organized. He worked 17 hours a day, seven days a week, for a year. Some sabbatical. At the end of the year, he had created one of the two great bone tumor pathology textbooks of the world. When you’re around values like Mirra’s, you want to pick up as much as you can.

学术界蕴含着许多可贵的价值。不久之前我就碰到一个例子。当时我以一家医院理事会主席的身份，与一位名叫约瑟夫·M·米拉401Joseph M. Mirra, MDJoseph M. Mirra , MD, is a bone and soft tissue pathologist in the Department of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center in Los Angeles. Dr. Mirra’s research interest is bone pathology, about which he has published more than 150 papers, produced 16 book chapters, and edited two books. Board-certified in anatomic and clinical pathology, Dr. Mirra is a sought-after visiting professor who also speaks nationally and internationally on bone pathology. He has been active in medical student teaching throughout his career and has participated in several symposia on bone tumor pathology.约瑟夫·M·米拉（Joseph M. Mirra）医学博士，是洛杉矶西达斯-西奈医学中心（Cedars-Sinai Medical Center）病理学与检验医学系的一位骨与软组织病理学家。米拉博士的研究兴趣是骨病理学，他已就此发表 150 多篇论文，撰写了 16 个图书章节，并编辑了两部著作。米拉博士拥有解剖病理学和临床病理学的专科认证，是一位备受欢迎的客座教授，还在国内外就骨病理学发表演讲。他整个职业生涯都积极参与医学生教学，并参加过多次骨肿瘤病理学专题讨论会。（Joseph M. Mirra）医学博士的医学院学者打交道。此人经过多年自律的工作，让自己对骨肿瘤病理学的了解超过了世界上几乎任何人。他希望把这套知识传下去，以帮助治疗骨癌。他打算怎么做呢？嗯，他决定写一本教科书；尽管我认为这类教科书销量不会超过几千册，但它们最终会出现在全世界各地的癌症治疗中心。他休了一年的学术假，坐在电脑前，把精心保存整理好的全部幻灯片调出来，每天工作17小时，每周工作7天，整整一年。这叫什么学术假。到了年底，他写出了世界上两部伟大的骨肿瘤病理学教科书之一。当你置身于米拉（Mirra）这样的价值氛围之中，你会想要尽可能多地汲取。

Another idea that was hugely useful to me was one I obtained when I listened in law school when some waggish professor said, “A legal mind is a mind that considers it feasible and useful, when two things are all twisted up together and interacting, to try to think about one thing without considering the other.”

另一个对我极有用的想法，是我在法学院听课时得来的。当时有位爱开玩笑的教授说：“所谓法律头脑，是指这样一种头脑：当两件事纠缠在一起、彼此影响时，它却认为可以只去想其中一件、而不考虑另一件，并且觉得这种做法既可行又管用。”

Well, I could see from that indirectly pejorative sentence that any such legal approach was ridiculous. And this pushed me further along in my natural drift, which was toward learning all the big ideas in all the big disciplines, so I wouldn’t be the perfect damn fool the professor described. And because the really big ideas carry about 95 percent of the freight, it wasn’t at all hard for me to pick up about 95 percent of what I needed from all the disciplines and to include use of this knowledge as a standard part of my mental routines.402Concert pianist钢琴演奏家

好吧，从那句带有贬义的间接评价里，我看出那种法律思路荒唐至极。这进一步推动了我天性的漂移——去研习所有重要学科里所有重大的思想，好让我不至于成为那位教授所描绘的十足的傻瓜。而由于真正重大的思想承载了大约95%的份量，我从各门学科汲取所需的约95%的知识，并把运用这些知识变成我思维程序中一个标准的部分，这并不算难。

Once you have the ideas, of course, you must continuously practice their use. Like a concert pianist, if you don’t practice you can’t perform well. So I went through life constantly practicing a multidisciplinary approach.

当然，一旦你有了这些思想，就必须持续地练习运用它们。就像音乐会上的钢琴家，不练习就弹不好。所以我这一生，都在不断地实践那种跨学科的方法。

Well, this habit has done a lot for me. It’s made life more fun. It’s made me more constructive. It’s made me more helpful to others. It’s made me richer than can be explained by any genetic gifts. My mental routine, properly practiced, really helps.

嗯，这个习惯让我获益良多。它让生活更有乐趣，让生活更具建设性，让我更能助人，也让我比任何天赋所能解释的还要富有。我的思维程序，只要得到恰当的实践，确实大有裨益。

Now, there are dangers in it because it works so well. If you use it, you will frequently find when you’re with some expert from another discipline—maybe even an expert who is your employer, with a vast ability to harm you—that you know more than he does about fitting his specialty to the problem at hand. You’ll sometimes see the correct answer when he’s missed it. That is a very dangerous position to be in. You can cause enormous offense by being right in a way that causes somebody else to lose face in his own discipline or hierarchy. I never found the perfect way to avoid harm from this serious problem. Even though I was a good poker player181Poker player扑克玩家 when I was young, I wasn’t good enough at pretending when I thought I knew more than my supervisors did. And I didn’t try as hard at pretending as would have been prudent. So I gave a lot of offense. Now, I’m generally tolerated as a harmless eccentric who will soon be gone. But coming up, I had a difficult period to go through.

不过，这习惯也有危险，因为它太管用了。如果你使用它，就常常会遇到这样的情形：当你和某位其他学科的专家——甚至可能是你的雇主、拥有严重伤害你的能力——在一起时，你会发现，关于如何将他的专业应用于眼前的问题，你比他懂得还多。有时他没看出的正确答案，你反倒看出来了。那可是一种非常危险的处境。你若以某种方式证明自己是对的，却让别的什么人在他自己的专业或等级体系里丢了面子，就会招来极大的冒犯。我从未找到能完美避开这个严重问题之伤害的办法。尽管我年轻时扑克玩得不错，但当我自认为比上司懂得多时，我却不太善于掩饰。我也没有像应有的审慎那样努力去掩饰。于是我得罪了很多人。如今，人们通常容忍我这个无害的怪老头，反正我很快就要走了。但在上升期，我确实经历过一段难熬的日子。

你若以某种方式证明自己是对的，却让别的什么人在他自己的专业或等级体系里丢了面子，就会招来极大的冒犯。

“You can cause enormous offense by being right in a way that causes somebody else to lose face in his own discipline or hierarchy.”当你以某种方式证明自己正确、却让另一个人在其专业或层级中丢了脸，你会招致极大的冒犯。

My advice to you is to be better than I was at keeping insights hidden. One of my colleagues, who graduated as number one in his class in law school and clerked at the US Supreme Court, tended as a young lawyer to show that he knew a lot. One day, the senior partner he was working under called him in and said, “Listen, Chuck, I want to explain something to you. Your duty is to behave in such a way that the client thinks he’s the smartest person in the room. If you have any energy or insight available after that, use it to make your senior partner look like the second-smartest person in the room. And only after you’ve satisfied those two obligations do you want your light to shine at all.”

我对你们的建议是：在隐藏洞见这一点上，要比当年的我做得更好。我有一位同事，法学院毕业时全班第一，还曾在美国最高法院（US Supreme Court）担任过法官助理；他年轻当律师时，总喜欢显摆自己懂得多。有一天，他那位资深合伙人把他叫进办公室说：“听好了，查克，我要跟你讲明白一件事。你的职责是：要让客户觉得，他是屋里最聪明的人。待你完成这桩任务、若还有余力或洞见，就用它来让你的资深合伙人显得像是屋里第二聪明的人。唯有履行了这两项义务之后，你才轮得到让自己发光。”

Well, that was a good system for rising in many a large law firm. But it wasn’t what I did. I usually moved with the drift of my nature, and if some other people didn’t like it, well, I didn’t need to be adored by everybody.

嗯，那倒是在许多大型律师事务所里往上爬的一套路数。但那不是我的做法。我通常随性而为，如果有人看不惯，那也没办法——我并不需要得到每个人的爱戴。

我通常随性而为，如果有人看不惯，那也没办法——我并不需要得到每个人的爱戴。

“I usually moved with the drift of my nature, and if some other people didn’t like it, well, I didn’t need to be adored by everybody.”我通常顺着自己的天性而行；若有人不喜欢，那也无妨——我不需要被所有人爱戴。

Let me further develop the idea that a multidisciplinary attitude is required if maturity is to be effective. Here I’m following a key idea of the greatest lawyer of antiquity, Marcus Tullius Cicero.404Marcus Tullius CiceroMarcus Tullius Cicero (106–43 BC) lived through the decline and fall of the Roman Republic and was important in many of the significant political events of his time. Besides being an orator, politician, and philosopher, Cicero was primarily a lawyer with a great respect for the lessons of history. He said: “History is the witness that testifies to the passing of time; it illumines reality, vitalizes memory, provides guidance in daily life, and brings us tidings of antiquity. To be ignorant of what happened before you were born is to be ever a child. For what is man’s lifetime unless the memory of past events is woven with those of earlier times?”马库斯·图利乌斯·西塞罗（Marcus Tullius Cicero，公元前 106–前 43 年）经历了罗马共和国的衰落与倾覆，是他那个时代许多重大政治事件中的重要人物。除了演说家、政治家和哲学家，西塞罗 归根到底是 是一名律师，对历史的教益怀着深深的敬意。他说：“历史是见证时间流逝的证人；它照亮现实、激活记忆、为日常生活提供指引，并给我们带来古代的消息。不知道自己出生之前发生过什么，就永远是个孩子。若非过往事件的记忆与更早时代的记忆交织在一起，人的一生又算得了什么？” Cicero is famous for saying that a man who doesn’t know what happened before he’s born goes through life like a child. That is a very correct idea. Cicero is right to ridicule somebody so foolish as not to know history. But if you generalize Cicero, as I think one should, there are a lot of other things that one should know in addition to history. And those other things are the big ideas in all the disciplines.

让我进一步展开这个观点：若要成熟而卓有成效，就必须具备跨学科的心态。在此，我遵循的是古代最伟大的律师马库斯·图利乌斯·西塞罗404Marcus Tullius CiceroMarcus Tullius Cicero (106–43 BC) lived through the decline and fall of the Roman Republic and was important in many of the significant political events of his time. Besides being an orator, politician, and philosopher, Cicero was primarily a lawyer with a great respect for the lessons of history. He said: “History is the witness that testifies to the passing of time; it illumines reality, vitalizes memory, provides guidance in daily life, and brings us tidings of antiquity. To be ignorant of what happened before you were born is to be ever a child. For what is man’s lifetime unless the memory of past events is woven with those of earlier times?”马库斯·图利乌斯·西塞罗（Marcus Tullius Cicero，公元前 106–前 43 年）经历了罗马共和国的衰落与倾覆，是他那个时代许多重大政治事件中的重要人物。除了演说家、政治家和哲学家，西塞罗 归根到底是 是一名律师，对历史的教益怀着深深的敬意。他说：“历史是见证时间流逝的证人；它照亮现实、激活记忆、为日常生活提供指引，并给我们带来古代的消息。不知道自己出生之前发生过什么，就永远是个孩子。若非过往事件的记忆与更早时代的记忆交织在一起，人的一生又算得了什么？”（Marcus Tullius Cicero）的一个核心思想。西塞罗有一句名言：一个对自己出生之前发生的事一无所知的人，终其一生都像个孩子。这是个非常正确的想法。西塞罗嘲笑那种蠢到不懂历史的人，是对的。但如果你像我认为应当做的那样，把西塞罗的话推广开去，就会发现除了历史，还有许多别的东西是应当知道的。而那些别的东西，就是所有学科里的重大思想。

And it doesn’t help you much just to know something well enough so that on one occasion you can prattle your way to an A in an exam. You have to learn many things in such a way that they’re in a mental latticework in your head and you automatically use them the rest of your life. If many of you try that, I solemnly promise that one day most will correctly come to think, “Somehow I’ve become one of the most effective people in my whole age cohort.” In contrast, if no effort is made toward such multidisciplinarity, many of the brightest of you who choose this course will live in the middle ranks, or in the shallows.

仅仅把某样东西学到足以在一次考试中夸夸其谈拿个A，对你助益不大。你必须把许多东西学到这样一种程度：让它们在你的头脑中织成一张格栅，并在余生中自动地运用它们。如果你们中有许多人去尝试，我郑重承诺：终有一天，大多数人会正确地意识到——“不知怎的，我竟成了同龄人中最有效率的人之一。”反之，若不对这种跨学科下功夫，你们当中许多选择了这条路的聪明人，将只能居于中游，或困于浅滩。

Another idea that I discovered was encapsulated by that story Dean McCaffery recounted earlier about the rustic who wanted to know where he was going to die so he wouldn’t go there.405Where he was going to die他将在何处离世 The rustic who had that ridiculous-sounding idea had a profound truth in his possession. The way complex adaptive systems work, and the way mental constructs work, problems frequently become easier to solve through inversion. If you turn problems around into reverse, you often think better. For instance, if you want to help India, the question you should consider asking is not “How can I help India?” Instead, you should ask, “How can I hurt India?” You find what will do the worst damage and then try to avoid it.

我发现的另一个想法，蕴含在麦卡弗里院长（Dean McCaffery）早先讲过的那个故事里：有个乡下人想知道自己会死在哪里，好让自己永不去那个地方。这个想法听起来荒唐的乡下人，其实掌握了一个深刻的真理。就复杂适应系统的运作方式，以及心智构造的运作方式而言，问题常常通过逆向思考而变得更容易求解。如果你把问题倒转过来，往往会想得更清楚。举例来说，如果你想帮助印度，你应当考虑的与其是“我怎样才能帮助印度？”，不如问：“我怎样才能伤害印度？”你找出会造成最严重损害的事，然后努力避开它。

如果你把问题倒转过来，往往会想得更清楚。

“If you turn problems around into reverse, you often think better.”如果你把问题倒过来想，往往能想得更清楚。

Perhaps the two approaches seem logically the same thing. But those who have mastered algebra406AlgebraThe word “ is derived from the Arabic word which appears in the treatise The Compendious Book on Calculation by Completion and Balancing, written in 820 by Persian mathematician Muḥammad ibn Mūsā al-Khwārizmī. The book provides systematic solutions of linear and quadratic equations.“代数”（algebra）一词源自阿拉伯语，见于波斯数学家穆罕默德·伊本·穆萨·花拉子米（Muḥammad ibn Mūsā al-Khwārizmī）公元 820 年所著的《化简与平衡计算手册》（The Compendious Book on Calculation by Completion and Balancing）。该书给出了一次方程和二次方程的系统解法。 know that inversion will often and easily solve problems that otherwise resist solution. And in life, just as in algebra, inversion will help you solve problems that you can’t otherwise handle.

也许这两种思路在逻辑上看起来是一回事。但精通代数的人都知道，逆向法常常能轻而易举地解出那些原本解不开的题。而在生活中，正如在代数中一样，逆向思考能帮你解决那些你原本无从下手的问题。

Let me use a little inversion now. What will really fail in life? What do we want to avoid? Some answers are easy. For example, sloth407Sloth懒惰 and unreliability will fail. If you’re unreliable, it doesn’t matter what your virtues are, you’re going to crater immediately. So faithfully doing what you’ve engaged to do should be an automatic part of your conduct. Of course you want to avoid sloth and unreliability.

现在让我来用一点逆向思考。人生中什么会真正导致失败？我们想要避开什么？有些答案很简单。比如，懒惰407Sloth懒惰和言而无信会导致失败。如果你言而无信，那么不管你有什么美德，都会立刻跌入谷底。所以，信守你许下的承诺，应当成为你行为中自动的一部分。当然，你要避开懒惰和言而无信。

Another thing to avoid is extremely intense ideology, because it cabbages up one’s mind.408Cabbages up one’s mind脑子里塞满卷心菜（愚钝） You see a lot of it in the worst of the TV preachers. They have different, intense, inconsistent ideas about technical theology, and a lot of them have minds reduced to cabbage. That can happen with political ideology. And if you’re young, it’s particularly easy to drift into intense and foolish political ideology and never get out.

另一件要避开的事，是极其强烈的意识形态，因为它会让人的头脑变成卷心菜。你在那些最糟糕的电视布道者身上能看到很多这样的例子。他们对技术性的神学持有各不相同、强烈而又自相矛盾的看法，其中许多人的脑子已经萎缩成了卷心菜。政治意识形态也会如此。而如果你还年轻，就特别容易陷入强烈而愚蠢的政治意识形态之中，再也走不出来。

When you announce that you’re a loyal member of some cult-like group and you start shouting out the orthodox ideology, what you’re doing is pounding it in, pounding it in, pounding it in. You’re ruining your mind, sometimes with startling speed. So you want to be very careful with intense ideology. It presents a big danger for the only mind you’re ever going to have.

当你宣布自己是某个类似邪教之团体的忠实成员，并开始高喊其正统意识形态时，你所做的，就是把那套东西往脑子里猛灌、猛灌、猛灌。你在毁掉自己的头脑，有时速度快得惊人。所以你要对强烈的意识形态格外小心。它对你仅有的一次头脑，构成了巨大的威胁。

“You want to be very careful with intense ideology. It presents a big danger for the only mind you’re ever going to get.”你得对狂热的意识形态万分小心。它对你此生唯一拥有的心智，构成了巨大的危险。

Darwin409Charles DarwinCharles Darwin (1809–1882) was a British naturalist whose teachings on evolution by natural selection revolutionized the science of biology. His book On the Origin of Species sold out immediately and was heavily attacked because it did not support the depiction of creation given in the Bible.查尔斯·达尔文（Charles Darwin，1809–1882 年）是英国博物学家，他关于自然选择进化的学说彻底改变了生物学。他的著作《物种起源》（On the Origin of Species）甫一出版即售罄，却因不支持《圣经》所描述的创世而遭到猛烈抨击。 formulated his theories on the transmutation of species in the late 1830s, but it was not until 1859 that he published his seminal work, On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection.410On the Origin of Species《物种起源》 Darwin accepted that any scientific theory proffering an alternative explanation to human origins would be met with widespread prejudice, and that therefore prudence dictated he become fully versed in every possible counterargument before publishing his ideas. Accordingly, he spent 20 years painstakingly cultivating his theory and preparing for its defense.

查尔斯·达尔文409Charles DarwinCharles Darwin (1809–1882) was a British naturalist whose teachings on evolution by natural selection revolutionized the science of biology. His book On the Origin of Species sold out immediately and was heavily attacked because it did not support the depiction of creation given in the Bible.查尔斯·达尔文（Charles Darwin，1809–1882 年）是英国博物学家，他关于自然选择进化的学说彻底改变了生物学。他的著作《物种起源》（On the Origin of Species）甫一出版即售罄，却因不支持《圣经》所描述的创世而遭到猛烈抨击。（Charles Darwin）在19世纪30年代末便形成了他的物种演变理论，但直到1859年才出版了他的开创性著作《论借助自然选择的物种起源》（On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection）。410On the Origin of Species《物种起源》达尔文明白，任何对人类起源给出另类解释的科学理论，都会遭遇普遍的偏见；因此审慎起见，他必须在发表自己的想法之前，把每一种可能的反驳都钻研透。于是，他花了20年心血，精心培育自己的理论，并为它的辩护做准备。

There is a warning example I use whenever I feel threatened by a drift toward intense political ideology. Some Scandinavian canoeists411Canoeists独木舟手 succeeded in getting through all the rapids of Scandinavia, and they thought they would continue their success by tackling the big whirlpools412Whirlpool漩涡 in northwest America. The death rate was 100 percent. A big whirlpool is something you want to avoid. And I think the same is true about intense ideology, particularly when your companions are all true believers.

每当我感到自己有滑向强烈政治意识形态的危险时，我就会用一个警示性的例子来提醒自己。一些斯堪的纳维亚的独木舟手411Canoeists独木舟手，成功穿越了斯堪的纳维亚的所有急流，便以为凭此也能去征服北美西北部的大漩涡412Whirlpool漩涡。结果死亡率是百分之百。大漩涡是你要避开的东西。而我认为，强烈的意识形态同样如此，尤其是当你的同伴全都是虔诚的信徒时。

I have what I call an iron prescription that helps me keep sane when I drift toward preferring one intense ideology over another. I feel that I’m not entitled to have an opinion unless I can state the arguments against my position better than the people who are in opposition. I think that I am qualified to speak only when I’ve reached that state.

我有一条所谓的“铁律”，当我偏向于偏爱某一种强烈意识形态、而非另一种时，它能帮我保持清醒。我觉得，除非我能够比反对者更好地陈述针对我立场的种种反驳，否则我无权持有某一观点。我认为，只有达到那种境界，我才配开口发言。

我觉得，除非我能够比反对者更好地陈述针对我立场的种种反驳，否则我无权持有某一观点。

“I feel that I’m not entitled to have an opinion unless I can state the arguments against my position better than the people who are in opposition.”我觉得，除非我能比反对者更精彩地陈述反对我立场的论点，否则我无权持有某个观点。

This sounds almost as extreme as the iron prescription Dean Acheson was fond of attributing to William the Silent of Orange, who roughly said, “It’s not necessary to hope in order to persevere.” That probably is too tough for most people, although I hope it won’t ever become too tough for me. My way of avoiding overintensity in ideology is easier than Acheson’s injunction and worth learning. This business of not drifting into extreme ideology is very, very important in life. If you want to end up wise, heavy ideology is very likely to prevent that outcome.

这话听起来，几乎和迪安·艾奇逊（Dean Acheson）喜欢归于奥兰治的沉默者威廉（William the Silent of Orange）的那条铁律一样极端；威廉大致说过：“要坚持，未必非得有希望。”对大多数人而言，这或许过于严苛，尽管我希望它对我永远不会变得过于严苛。我这种避免意识形态过度强烈的方法，比艾奇逊的戒律更轻松，也值得学习。这种不滑入极端意识形态的事，在人生中非常、非常重要。如果你想最终变得有智慧，浓厚的意识形态极可能让你事与愿违。

Another thing that often causes folly and ruin is the self-serving bias, often subconscious, to which we’re all subject. You think that “the true little me” is entitled to do what it wants to do. For instance, why shouldn’t the true little me get what it wants by overspending its income?

另一件常常招致愚蠢与毁灭的事，是我们人人都难免受其影响的“自我服务偏差”——它往往是潜意识的。你会认为“那个真实的、小小的我”有权去做它想做的事。比如，那个真实的、小小的我，凭什么不能通过透支收入来得到它想要的东西呢？

Well, there once was a man who became the most famous composer in the world, but he was utterly miserable most of the time. One of the reasons was that he always overspent his income. That was Mozart.415MozartThe notion of as an impoverished composer comes primarily from a series of letters he wrote from 1788 to 1791 to his Masonic brother Michael Puchberg asking for loans. Other evidence suggests Mozart’s income, though subject to considerable fluctuation, was unusually high for a musician, placing him during some years in the top 10 percent of all Vienna inhabitants. Economists William and Hilda Baumol, on the other hand, calculate that Mozart’s income in the last decade of his life was middle-class at 3,000–4,000 florins a year (about $30,000–$40,000 in 1990). What happened to Mozart’s money? Mozart’s sickly wife, Constanze, required regular cures at spring baths used only by the wealthy. During lean times, the Mozarts continued to live in their accustomed style, giving themselves cash flow problems. The situation was exacerbated by their failure to save any money during flush periods and by a judgment against Mozart in 1791 resulting from a suit brought by Prince Karl Lichnowsky. Some scholars also cite evidence that Mozart gambled at billiards and cards.莫扎特（Mozart）作为穷困作曲家的印象，主要来自他 1788 年至 1791 年间写给共济会兄弟迈克尔·普赫伯格（Michael Puchberg）求借的一系列信。其他证据表明，莫扎特的收入尽管波动相当大，对一位音乐家而言却高得异常，有些年份跻身维也纳所有居民的前 10%。另一方面，经济学家威廉和希尔达·鲍莫尔（William and Hilda Baumol）测算，莫扎特生命最后十年的收入属中产阶级水平，为每年 3,000–4,000 弗罗林（约合 1990 年的 3 万–4 万美元）。莫扎特的钱去哪儿了？他体弱多病的妻子康斯坦策（Constanze）需要定期到只有富人才能使用的温泉疗养地疗养。拮据时，莫扎特夫妇依旧过着习以为常的阔绰生活，给自己造成了现金流问题。宽裕时不存钱，以及 1791 年卡尔·利赫诺夫斯基亲王（Prince Karl Lichnowsky）提起诉讼导致的一项不利判决，使局面雪上加霜。一些学者还举出证据，称莫扎特曾赌博桌球和纸牌。 If Mozart couldn’t get by with this kind of asinine conduct, I don’t think you should try it.

嗯，从前有个人，成了全世界最著名的作曲家，可他大半时光都极其悲惨。原因之一，就是他总是入不敷出。那人是莫扎特414Mozart莫扎特（Mozart）。连莫扎特都混不过这种蠢行，我想你也不该去试。

连莫扎特414Mozart莫扎特都混不过这种蠢行，我想你也不该去试。

“If Mozart couldn’t get by with this kind of asinine conduct, I don’t think you should try it.”连莫扎特都靠这种蠢行混不下去，我想你也不该去试。

Generally speaking, envy, resentment, revenge, and self-pity416Envy, resentment, revenge, and self-pity嫉妒、怨恨、报复与自怜 are disastrous modes of thought. Self-pity can get pretty close to paranoia.417Paranoia偏执狂 Paranoia is one of the very hardest things to reverse. You do not want to drift into self-pity. I had a friend who carried a thick stack of linen-based cards. When somebody would make a comment that reflected self-pity, he would slowly and portentously pull out his huge stack of cards, take the top one, and hand it to the person. The card said, “Your story has touched my heart. Never have I heard of anyone with as many misfortunes as you.”

总的说来，妒忌、怨恨、报复与自怜，都是灾难性的思维方式。自怜几乎可以逼近偏执。417Paranoia偏执狂而偏执是最难逆转的东西之一。你不要滑入自怜之中。我有一位朋友，随身带着厚厚一叠亚麻卡片。每当有人说出带着自怜意味的话，他就会缓慢而庄严地掏出那一大叠卡片，抽出最上面一张，递给那人。卡片上写着：“你的故事打动了我心。我从未听说过有谁像你这般多灾多难。”

Well, you can say that’s waggery, but I suggest it can be mental hygiene. Every time you find you’re drifting into self-pity, whatever the cause, even if your child is dying of cancer, self-pity is not going to help. Just give yourself one of my friend’s cards. Self-pity is always counterproductive. It’s the wrong way to think. And when you avoid it you get a great advantage over everybody else, or almost everybody else, because self-pity is a standard response. And you can train yourself out of it.

嗯，你可以说那是玩笑，但我倒觉得那是一种精神卫生。每当你发现自己正在滑入自怜——无论出于什么原因，哪怕你的孩子正死于癌症——自怜都无济于事。不妨给自己一张我朋友的卡片。自怜永远适得其反，那是一种错误的思维方式。而当你避开它时，你就获得了相对于其他人、或几乎其他所有人的巨大优势，因为自怜是一种标准的反应。而且你可以训练自己摆脱它。

Of course, you also want to get self-serving bias out of your mental routines. Thinking that what’s good for you is good for the wider civilization and rationalizing foolish or evil conduct based on your subconscious tendency to serve yourself is a terrible way to think. You want to drive that out of yourself because you want to be wise, not foolish, and good, not evil.

当然，你还要把自我服务偏差从你的思维程序中清除出去。认为对你有利的就是对整个文明有利，并基于你那服务于自我的潜意识倾向，去为愚蠢或邪恶的行径找借口——那是一种糟糕透顶的思维方式。你要将这种念头从自身驱除，因为你想成为智者而非愚人，想为善而非作恶。

You also have to allow, in your own cognition and conduct, for the self-serving bias of everybody else, because most people are not going to be very successful at removing such bias, the human condition being what it is. If you don’t allow for self-serving bias in the conduct of others, you are, again, a fool.

你还必须在自己的认知与行为中，容许其他人也带有自我服务偏差，因为以人性的现状而论，大多数人都不大能成功地清除这种偏差。如果你在别人的行为中不容许自我服务偏差的存在，那你又是个傻瓜。

如果你在别人的行为中不容许自我服务偏差的存在，那你又是个傻瓜。

“If you don’t allow for self-serving bias in the conduct of others, you are, again, a fool.”倘若你不体察他人行为中的自我服务偏见，那你又是个傻子。

I watched the brilliant and worthy Harvard Law Review–trained general counsel of Salomon Brothers lose his career there. When the able CEO [John Gutfreund]418John GutfreundJohn Gutfreund (1929–2016) , chairman and CEO of Salomon Brothers, paid a high price for inaction when he was put on notice of company misdeeds. In 1991, a Salomon trader made an illegal $3.2 billion bid for US treasury securities. Although the transaction was reported to top management only days later, Gutfreund did not take the warning seriously and failed to report it for more than three months. Gutfreund knew as soon as the matter came out in the press that his delay in reporting had torpedoed his 38-year career with Salomon. He called in one of Salomon’s outside directors, Warren Buffett, to save the company and restore its reputation. Buffett handled the complicated project masterfully, and the firm survived and prospered; it was later sold for $9 billion to Travelers.约翰·古特弗罗因德（John Gutfreund，1929–2016 年），所罗门兄弟（Salomon Brothers）的董事长兼 CEO，在被告知公司不法行为后因不作为而付出了高昂代价。1991 年，一位所罗门交易员对美国国债进行了 32 亿美元的非法投标。尽管此事仅在数日后就报到了最高管理层，古特弗罗因德却没有认真对待这个警告，逾三个月未予上报。他心里清楚，此事一见报，他延迟上报就把他与所罗门 38 年的职业生涯炸毁了。他请来所罗门的一位外部董事沃伦·巴菲特挽救公司、恢复声誉。巴菲特出色地处理了这个复杂局面，公司起死回生并日益兴旺；后来以 90 亿美元卖给了旅行者集团（Travelers）。 was told that an underling had done something wrong, the general counsel said, “Gee, we don’t have any legal duty to report this, but I think it’s what we should do. It’s our moral duty.”

我曾亲眼看着所罗门兄弟（Salomon Brothers）那位聪慧而可敬、受训于《哈佛法律评论》（Harvard Law Review）的总法律顾问，在那里断送了自己的职业生涯。当那位能干的CEO被告知有下属做了错事时，总法律顾问说：“哎呀，我们在法律上并没有义务汇报这件事，但我认为那是我们应当做的。那是我们的道德责任。”

The general counsel was technically and morally correct, but his approach didn’t persuade. He recommended a very unpleasant thing for the busy CEO to do and the CEO, quite understandably, put the issue off, and put it off, not with any intent to do wrong. In due course, when powerful regulators resented not having been promptly informed, down went the CEO and the general counsel with him.

这位总法律顾问在法律上和道德上都站得住脚，但他的方式却没能说服人。他给那位忙碌的CEO提了一个极其不愉快的建议，而CEO——完全可以理解地——把这件事一拖再拖，倒也并非存心做错。时机一到，当有权势的监管者因未被及时告知而恼怒时，CEO倒了，总法律顾问也跟着倒了。

The correct persuasive technique in situations like that was given by Ben Franklin. He said, “If you would persuade, appeal to interest, not to reason.” The self-serving bias of man is extreme, and should have been used in attaining the correct outcome. So the general counsel should have said, “Look, this is likely to erupt into something that will destroy you, take away your money, take away your status, grossly impair your reputation. My recommendation will prevent a likely disaster from which you can’t recover.” That approach would have worked. You should often appeal to interest, not to reason, even when your motives are lofty.

在这种情形下，本·富兰克林419Ben Franklin本·富兰克林（Ben Franklin）给出了正确的说服技巧。他说：“若要说服人，诉诸利益，而非诉诸理性。”

人的自我服务偏差是极端的，本应被用来达成正确的结果。所以那位总法律顾问本该说：“听着，这事很可能爆发成某种会毁掉你的东西——夺走你的金钱，夺走你的地位，严重损害你的声誉。我的建议，能防止一场你无法挽回的灾难。”那样才管用。你应当常常诉诸利益，而非诉诸理性，哪怕你的动机是崇高的。

Another thing to avoid is being subjected to perverse incentives. You don’t want to be in a perverse incentive system that’s rewarding you if you behave more and more foolishly, or worse and worse. Perverse incentives are so powerful as controllers of human cognition and human behavior that one should avoid their influence. One of the things you’re going to find in at least a few modern law firms is high billable-hour quotas. I could not have lived under billable-hour quotas of 2,400 hours a year. That would have caused too many problems for me. I wouldn’t have done it. I don’t have a solution for the situation some of you will face. You’ll have to figure out for yourselves how to handle such significant problems.

另一件要避开的事，是受制于反常的激励机制。你不会想置身于这样一种反常激励系统：你表现得越蠢、或越来越糟，它给你的回报反而越多。反常的激励机制，作为对人类认知与行为的控制力量，实在太过强大，人应当避开它的影响。在至少几家现代律师事务所里，你会看到高得离谱的计费工时定额。我可没法在每年2400小时计费工时的定额下活下去。那会给我惹出太多麻烦。我不会接受那种条件。对于你们当中某些人将面临的这种局面，我给不出解决方案。你们得自己琢磨，该如何应对这类重大问题。

Perverse associations are also to be avoided. You particularly want to avoid working directly under somebody you don’t admire and don’t want to be like. It’s dangerous. We’re all subject to control to some extent by authority figures, particularly authority figures who are rewarding us. Dealing properly with this danger requires both some talent and will.

反常的人际关系也要避开。你尤其要避开的，是在一个你既不敬仰、也不想成为其那样的人手下直接干活。那很危险。我们在某种程度上都受权威人物——尤其是那些给我们回报的权威人物——的控制。要妥善应对这种危险，既需要些才华，也需要意志。

避免在一个你既不敬仰、也不想成为其那样的人手下直接干活。

“Avoid working directly under somebody you don’t admire and don’t want to be like.”419Ben Franklin本·富兰克林避免直接为你不钦佩、也不想成为的人工作。（本杰明·富兰克林）

I coped in my time by identifying people I admired and by maneuvering, mostly without criticizing anybody, so that I was usually working under the right sort of people. A lot of law firms will permit that if you’re shrewd enough to work it out with some tact. Generally, your outcome in life will be more satisfactory if you work under people you correctly admire.

在我那个年代，我的应对之道是：找出我敬仰的人，并通过周旋——大多不批评任何人——让自己通常能在那类合适的人手下工作。如果你足够精明、能委婉地把事情安排妥当，许多律师事务所是允许的。一般而言，在你由衷敬仰的人手下工作，你的人生结果会更令人满意。

Engaging in routines that allow you to maintain objectivity are, of course, very helpful to cognition. We all remember that Darwin paid special attention to disconfirming evidence, particularly when it disconfirmed something he believed and loved. Routines like that are required if a life is to maximize correct thinking.

养成一些能让你保持客观公正的常规，当然对认知极有帮助。我们都记得，达尔文（Charles Darwin）特别留意反证，尤其是当反证否定了他所信奉并挚爱的东西时。若想让一生中的正确思考最大化，就需要这样的常规。

One also needs checklist routines.420Checklist routines检查清单惯例 They prevent a lot of errors, and not just for pilots. You should not only possess wide-ranging elementary wisdom but also go through mental checklist routines in using it. There is no other procedure that will work as well.

人还需要核查清单式的常规。它们能防止大量错误，而且不光是对飞行员而言。你不仅应当具备广博的基础智慧，还应当在使用它时，走一遍头脑中的核查清单。没有别的程序能取得同样好的效果。

Another idea that I found important is that maximizing non-egality will often work wonders. What do I mean? Well, John Wooden421John Wooden约翰·伍登 of UCLA presented an instructive example when he was the number one basketball coach in the world. He said to the bottom five players, “You don’t get to play; you are practice partners.” The top seven did almost all the playing. Well, the top seven learned more—remember the importance of the learning machine—because they were doing all the playing. And when he adopted that non-egalitarian system, Wooden won more games than he had won before.

我发现的另一个重要想法是：把不平等最大化，常常能创造奇迹。这是什么意思呢？嗯，加州大学洛杉矶分校（UCLA）的约翰·伍登421John Wooden约翰·伍登（John Wooden）就提供了一个富有教益的范例——那时他是世界上头号篮球教练。他对水平最差的五名队员说：“你们上不了场；你们是陪练。”上场打球几乎全是那七名尖子。嗯，那七名尖子学到的更多——别忘了学习机器的重要性——因为他们包揽了所有的上场时间。而当他采用那种非平等主义的体制时，伍登赢下的比赛比从前更多了。

I think the game of competitive life often requires maximizing the experience of the people who have the most aptitude and the most determination as learning machines. And if you want the very highest reaches of human achievement, that’s where you have to go. You do not want to choose a brain surgeon for your child by drawing straws to select one of 50 applicants, all of whom take turns doing procedures. You don’t want your airplanes designed in too egalitarian a fashion. You don’t want your Berkshire Hathaways run that way either. You want to provide a lot of playing time for your best players.

我认为，竞争性的生活这场游戏，往往要求让那些最有天资、最有决心成为学习机器的人，最大限度地积累经验。而如果你想抵达人类成就的最高峰，那就必须走这条路。你不会想用抽签的方式，从50名申请人中抓一个来给自己的孩子做脑部外科手术，而让他们轮流主刀。你不会想让你的飞机以一种过于平等主义的方式设计出来。你也不会想让你的伯克希尔·哈撒韦（Berkshire Hathaway）以那种方式经营。你要让你最优秀的“球员”获得大量的“上场时间”。

你不会想让你的飞机以一种过于平等主义的方式设计出来。你也不会想让你的伯克希尔·哈撒韦（Berkshire Hathaway）以那种方式经营。

“You don’t want your airplanes designed in too egalitarian a fashion. You don’t want your Berkshire Hathaways run that way either.”你不会希望你的飞机以过分平等主义的方式设计。你也不该让伯克希尔·哈撒韦以那种方式运转。

I frequently tell the apocryphal story about how Max Planck,422Max PlanckBorn in Germany to a law professor father, Max Planck (1858–1947) earned his doctorate at age 21. His earliest work on thermodynamics evolved into an interest in radiation. From these studies, he was led to work on the distribution of energy in the spectrum of radiation. Planck’s work on energy emissions was essential to the field of physics and came to be known as quantum theory. He was awarded the Nobel Prize for Physics in 1918.马克斯·普朗克（Max Planck，1858–1947 年）生于德国，父亲是法学教授，21 岁就获得博士学位。他最早关于热力学的研究，渐渐引向对辐射的兴趣。从这些研究出发，他投入到辐射谱中能量分布的工作。普朗克关于能量发射的工作对物理学领域至关重要，后来被称为量子理论。1918 年，他被授予诺贝尔物理学奖。 after he won the Nobel Prize, went around Germany giving the same standard lecture on the new quantum mechanics. Over time, his chauffeur423Chauffeur knowledge司机式知识（鹦鹉学舌） memorized the lecture and said, “Would you mind, Professor Planck, because it’s so boring to stay in our routine, if I gave the lecture in Munich and you just sat in front wearing my chauffeur’s hat?” Planck said, “Why not?” And the chauffeur got up and gave this long lecture on quantum mechanics, after which a physics professor stood up and asked a perfectly ghastly question. The speaker said, “Well, I’m surprised that in an advanced city like Munich I get such an elementary question. I’m going to ask my chauffeur to reply.”

我常常讲那个未必可靠的传说：马克斯·普朗克422Max PlanckBorn in Germany to a law professor father, Max Planck (1858–1947) earned his doctorate at age 21. His earliest work on thermodynamics evolved into an interest in radiation. From these studies, he was led to work on the distribution of energy in the spectrum of radiation. Planck’s work on energy emissions was essential to the field of physics and came to be known as quantum theory. He was awarded the Nobel Prize for Physics in 1918.马克斯·普朗克（Max Planck，1858–1947 年）生于德国，父亲是法学教授，21 岁就获得博士学位。他最早关于热力学的研究，渐渐引向对辐射的兴趣。从这些研究出发，他投入到辐射谱中能量分布的工作。普朗克关于能量发射的工作对物理学领域至关重要，后来被称为量子理论。1918 年，他被授予诺贝尔物理学奖。（Max Planck）获得诺贝尔奖之后，走遍德国，一遍遍讲着关于新量子力学的同一套标准讲座。久而久之，他的司机423Chauffeur knowledge司机式知识（鹦鹉学舌）把讲座背了下来，说：“普朗克教授，咱们的老一套实在无聊，您介不介意，让我在慕尼黑讲那场，您就坐在前排、戴着我的司机帽？”普朗克说：“有何不可？”于是司机走上台，发表了一通关于量子力学的长篇大论；接着一位物理学教授站起来，提了一个极其刁钻的问题。演讲者说：“嗯，真没想到，在慕尼黑这样先进的城市，竟会有人问出这么基础的问题。我打算让我的司机来回答。”

Well, the reason I tell that story is not to celebrate the quick-wittedness of the protagonist. In this world, I think we have two kinds of knowledge. One is Planck knowledge, that of the people who really know. They’ve paid the dues, they have the aptitude. Then we’ve got chauffeur knowledge. They have learned to prattle the talk. They may have a big head of hair. They often have a fine timbre in their voices. They make a big impression. But in the end, what they’ve got is chauffeur knowledge masquerading as real knowledge. I think I’ve just described practically every politician in the United States. You’re going to have the problem in your life of getting as much responsibility as you can to the people with the Planck knowledge and away from the people who have the chauffeur knowledge. And there are huge forces working against you.

嗯，我讲这个故事，可不是为了赞美主角的机敏。我认为，在这个世界上，知识有两种。一种是普朗克知识，属于那些真正懂行的人。他们下了功夫，也有天资。另一种则是司机知识。他们学会了鹦鹉学舌。他们也许有一头浓密的头发。他们往往有一副悦耳的嗓音。他们给人留下深刻印象。但说到底，他们拥有的，是伪装成真才实学的司机知识。我想，我刚才几乎把美国所有的政客都描绘了一遍。在你的人生中，你会遇到这样一个难题：要尽可能多地把责任，交给拥有普朗克知识的人，而远离那些只有司机知识的人。而且，有巨大的力量在与你作对。

My generation has failed you to some extent. More and more, we’re delivering to you in California a legislature in which mostly the certified nuts from the left and the certified nuts from the right424Certified nuts from the left and the right左右两派的认证疯子 are the ones allowed to serve. And none of them are removable. That’s what my generation has done for you. But you wouldn’t like it to be too easy, would you?

在某种程度上，我们这一代辜负了你们。我们交到你们手里的，是加利福尼亚州一个越来越这样的立法机构：获准任职的，大多是左派的货真价实的疯子，以及右派的货真价实的疯子。而且他们谁也撤不掉。这就是我们这一代人为你们做的事。不过，你们大概也不希望事情太容易，对吧？

Another thing that I have found is that intense interest in any subject is indispensable if you’re really going to excel in it. I could force myself to be fairly good in a lot of things, but I couldn’t excel in anything in which I didn’t have an intense interest. So, to some extent, you’re going to have to do as I did. If at all feasible, you want to maneuver yourself into doing something in which you have an intense interest.

我发现的另一件事是：如果你真想在某个领域出类拔萃，那么对它怀有强烈的兴趣，是不可或缺的。许多事情我都能逼自己做得相当好，但我无法在没有强烈兴趣的事情上做到卓越。所以，在某种程度上，你们也得像我一样。只要可行，你们就要设法让自己去做一件你怀有强烈兴趣的事。

Another thing you have to do is have a lot of assiduity. I like that word because to me it means “Sit down on your ass until you do it.” I’ve had marvelous partners, full of assiduity, all my life. I think I got them partly because I tried to deserve them and partly because I was shrewd enough to select them, and partly there was some luck.

你们还须做的另一件事，是要有极大的勤勉。我喜欢这个词，因为对我而言，它意味着“屁股钉在椅子上，直到把事情做完”。我这一生，都有极好的、充满勤勉的合伙人相伴。我想我得到他们，部分是因为我努力让自己配得上他们，部分是因为我足够精明地选择了他们，还有部分是因为运气。

你们还须做的另一件事，是要有极大的勤勉。我喜欢这个词，因为对我而言，它意味着“屁股钉在椅子上，直到把事情做完”。

“Another thing you have to do is have a lot of assiduity. I like that word because to me it means ‘Sit down on your ass until you do it.’”你还得做的另一件事，是要有十足的勤勉（assiduity）。我喜欢这个词，因为对我而言，它意味着『屁股坐在椅子上，直到你把事做成。』

Two partners that I chose for one phase in my life made the following simple agreement when they created a little design-and-build construction team in the middle of the Great Depression: “Two-man partnership,” they said, “and divide everything equally. And whenever we’re behind in our commitments to other people, we will both work 14 hours a day, seven days a week, until we’re caught up.” Well, needless to say that firm didn’t fail, and my partners were widely admired. Simple, old-fashioned ideas like theirs are almost sure to provide a good outcome.

在我人生的某个阶段，我挑选的两位合伙人，在大萧条（Great Depression）中期组建了一支小型的“设计—建造”施工队，当时他们定下了如下简单的约定：“两人合伙，”他们说，“一切平分。而每当我们对别人的承诺有所拖欠，我们就两人都每天工作14小时、每周工作7天，直到赶上进度。”嗯，不用说，那家公司没有失败，而我的合伙人也广受敬重。像他们那样朴素而老派的理念，几乎注定会带来好的结果。

Another thing to cope with is that life is very likely to provide terrible blows, unfair blows. Some people recover and others don’t. There I think the attitude of Epictetus425EpictetusEven though he was born a slave in Hierapolis and endured a permanent physical disability, (55–135) maintained that all human beings are perfectly free to control their own lives and to live in harmony with nature. After intense study of the traditional Stoic curriculum of logic, physics, and ethics, Epictetus spent his entire career teaching philosophy and promoting a daily regime of rigorous self-examination. He eventually gained his freedom but was exiled from Rome by Domitian in 89.爱比克泰德（Epictetus，55–135 年）虽生于希拉波利斯、身为奴隶，且身有终身残疾，却主张所有人都完全有自由掌控自己的生活、与自然和谐共处。在深入研习逻辑学、物理学和伦理学的传统斯多葛课程之后，爱比克泰德毕生致力于教授哲学，并倡导每日严格自省的习惯。他最终获得了自由，却在公元 89 年被多米提安（Domitian）逐出罗马。 helps guide one to the right reaction. He thought that every mischance in life, however bad, created an opportunity to behave well. He believed every mischance provided an opportunity to learn something useful, and one’s duty was not to become immersed in self-pity but to utilize each terrible blow in a constructive fashion. His ideas were very sound, influencing the best of the Roman emperors, Marcus Aurelius and many others over many centuries. And you may remember the epitaph that Epictetus made for himself: “Here lies Epictetus, a slave, maimed in body, the ultimate in poverty, and favored by the gods.”

另一件要应付的事是：生活很可能给你沉重的、不公平的打击。有的人挺了过来，有的人没有。在这方面，我认为爱比克泰德425EpictetusEven though he was born a slave in Hierapolis and endured a permanent physical disability, (55–135) maintained that all human beings are perfectly free to control their own lives and to live in harmony with nature. After intense study of the traditional Stoic curriculum of logic, physics, and ethics, Epictetus spent his entire career teaching philosophy and promoting a daily regime of rigorous self-examination. He eventually gained his freedom but was exiled from Rome by Domitian in 89.爱比克泰德（Epictetus，55–135 年）虽生于希拉波利斯、身为奴隶，且身有终身残疾，却主张所有人都完全有自由掌控自己的生活、与自然和谐共处。在深入研习逻辑学、物理学和伦理学的传统斯多葛课程之后，爱比克泰德毕生致力于教授哲学，并倡导每日严格自省的习惯。他最终获得了自由，却在公元 89 年被多米提安（Domitian）逐出罗马。（Epictetus）的态度，有助于引导人作出正确的反应。他认为，生活中每一次不幸，无论多糟，都创造了一个行善的机会。他相信，每一次不幸都提供了一个学习有用之物的机会，而人的职责，不是沉溺于自怜，而是以建设性的方式，利用每一次沉重的打击。他的想法非常健全，影响了最优秀的罗马皇帝马库斯·奥勒留（Marcus Aurelius）以及此后许多世纪里的许多人。你们或许还记得爱比克泰德（Epictetus）为自己拟的墓志铭：“此处长眠着爱比克泰德，一个奴隶，身体残缺，穷困至极，却蒙诸神眷顾。”

Well, that’s the way Epictetus is now remembered: favored by the gods. He was favored because he became wise, became manly, and instructed others, both in his own time and over following centuries.

嗯，爱比克泰德（Epictetus）如今正是以这种方式被铭记的：蒙诸神眷顾。他之所以被眷顾，是因为他变得智慧，变得有男子气概，并且教诲了他人——无论在他自己的时代，还是在其后的许多世纪。

I’ve another idea to emphasize in a brief account. My grandfather Munger426Thomas Charles MungerThomas Charles Munger (1861–1941) was born in Fletcher, Ohio, on the eve of the Civil War. His parents, itinerant farmers and schoolteachers, were so impoverished that as a child Judge Munger recalled trips to the butcher shop with 5\xa2 in his pocket to buy the lowest forms of animal parts the butcher had to offer. Despite this unfortunate beginning, Judge Munger managed to acquire an outstanding education owing both to his parents’ efforts and his own autodidacticism. He was appointed United States District Judge by President Theodore Roosevelt in 1907 and became well known for both his industrious approach to legal research and the clear and concise form of his judicial opinions.托马斯·查尔斯·芒格（Thomas Charles Munger，1861–1941 年）生于俄亥俄州弗莱彻，正值内战前夕。他的父母是四处漂泊的农民和乡村教师，家境如此贫寒，以至于芒格法官小时候回忆，自己口袋里揣着 5 美分去肉店，买屠夫能提供的最低档的动物部件。尽管起步不幸，芒格法官凭借父母的努力和自己的自学成才，获得了出色的教育。1907 年，他被西奥多·罗斯福总统任命为美国联邦地区法官，并因法律研究的勤勉，以及司法意见书清晰简洁的形式而闻名。 was the only federal judge in his city for nearly 40 years. I admired him. I’m his namesake. And I’m Confucian enough that even now, as I speak, I’m thinking, “Well, Judge Munger would be pleased to have me here.” All these years after my grandfather is dead, I conceive myself as duty-bound to carry the torch for my grandfather’s values. One such value was prudence as the servant of duty. Grandfather Munger was a federal judge at a time when there were no pensions for widows of federal judges. So if he didn’t save from his income, my grandmother would become a destitute widow. And besides, net worth would enable him to serve others better. Being the kind of man he was, he underspent his income all his life and left his widow in comfortable circumstances.

还有一点想法，我想简明地强调一下。我的祖父芒格426Thomas Charles MungerThomas Charles Munger (1861–1941) was born in Fletcher, Ohio, on the eve of the Civil War. His parents, itinerant farmers and schoolteachers, were so impoverished that as a child Judge Munger recalled trips to the butcher shop with 5\xa2 in his pocket to buy the lowest forms of animal parts the butcher had to offer. Despite this unfortunate beginning, Judge Munger managed to acquire an outstanding education owing both to his parents’ efforts and his own autodidacticism. He was appointed United States District Judge by President Theodore Roosevelt in 1907 and became well known for both his industrious approach to legal research and the clear and concise form of his judicial opinions.托马斯·查尔斯·芒格（Thomas Charles Munger，1861–1941 年）生于俄亥俄州弗莱彻，正值内战前夕。他的父母是四处漂泊的农民和乡村教师，家境如此贫寒，以至于芒格法官小时候回忆，自己口袋里揣着 5 美分去肉店，买屠夫能提供的最低档的动物部件。尽管起步不幸，芒格法官凭借父母的努力和自己的自学成才，获得了出色的教育。1907 年，他被西奥多·罗斯福总统任命为美国联邦地区法官，并因法律研究的勤勉，以及司法意见书清晰简洁的形式而闻名。（Munger），曾在他的城市里做了将近40年唯一的联邦法官。我敬仰他。我与他是同名。而且我深受儒家思想熏陶，以至于即便此刻，我在演讲时也在想：“嗯，芒格法官（Judge Munger）会很高兴我站在这里。”祖父离世这么多年后，我仍认为自己责无旁贷，要接过他价值观的火炬。他的价值观之一，便是：审慎，是责任的仆人。芒格爷爷担任联邦法官时，联邦法官的遗孀是没有抚恤金的。所以如果他不从收入中储蓄，我的祖母就会变成一个一贫如洗的寡妇。此外，净资产也能让他更好地服务他人。以他那种为人，他终其一生量入为出，给遗孀留下了宽裕的生活境况。

But that was not all that his prudence enabled. Along the way, in the ’30s, my uncle’s tiny bank failed and couldn’t reopen without help. My grandfather saved the bank by exchanging over a third of his good assets for horrible bank assets. I’ve always remembered the event. It reminds me of [A. E.] Housman’s427A. E. HousmanA·E·豪斯曼 little poem that went something like this:

但这还不是他的审慎所成就的全部。中途，在20世纪30年代，我叔叔的小银行倒闭了，若没有外力相助便无法重开。我的祖父用自己超过三分之一的优良资产，去交换那家银行糟糕透顶的资产，从而拯救了它。这件事我一直记着。它让我想起豪斯曼427A. E. HousmanA·E·豪斯曼（Houseman）的一首小诗，大意是这样的：

You may well say, “Who wants to go through life anticipating trouble?” Well, I did, trained as I was. I’ve gone through a long life anticipating trouble. And here I am now, well along in my 84th year. Like Epictetus, I’ve had a favored life. It didn’t make me unhappy to anticipate trouble all the time and be ready to perform adequately if trouble came. It didn’t hurt me at all. In fact, it helped me. So I quitclaim to you Housman and Judge Munger.

我这一生都在预期麻烦的到来。

“I’ve gone through a long life anticipating trouble.”我这一生，都在预期麻烦的到来。

The last idea that I want to give to you, as you go out into a profession that frequently puts a lot of procedure and some mumbo-jumbo into what it does, is that complex bureaucratic procedure does not represent the highest form civilization can reach. One higher form is a seamless, non-bureaucratic web of deserved trust. Not much fancy procedure, just totally reliable people correctly trusting one another. That’s the way an operating room works at the Mayo Clinic.428Mayo Clinic梅奥诊所 If lawyers would introduce a lot of lawyer-like process, more patients would die. So never forget, when you’re a lawyer, that while you may have to sell procedure, you don’t always have to buy. In your own life, what you want to maximize is a seamless web of deserved trust. And if your proposed marriage contract has 47 pages, my suggestion is that you not enter.

我要交给你们的最后一点想法是：你们即将步入一个常常在行事中塞进大量程序和些许胡言乱语的行业；而复杂官僚化的程序，并不代表文明所能达到的最高形态。一种更高的形态，是一张无缝的、非官僚的、应得信任之网。没有多少花哨的程序，只有完全可靠的人，彼此正确地信任。梅奥诊所428Mayo Clinic梅奥诊所（Mayo Clinic）的手术室的运作方式便是如此。如果律师们把许多律师式的流程引进去，会有更多病人死掉。所以，当你身为律师时，永远别忘了：你或许不得不兜售程序，却不必总是照单全收。在你自己的人生中，你想要最大化的，是一张无缝的应得信任之网。而如果你们拟定的婚姻契约长达47页，我的建议是：这婚还是不结为好。

在你自己的人生中，你想要最大化的，是一张无缝的应得信任之网。

“In your own life, what you want to maximize is a seamless web of deserved trust.”在你自己的人生里，你所要最大化的，是一张无缝的、当之无愧的信任之网。

Well, that’s enough for one graduation. I hope these ruminations of an old man are useful to you. In the end, I’m speaking toward the only outcome feasible for old Valiant-for-Truth in Pilgrim’s Progress:429Pilgrim’s ProgressThe Pilgrim’s Progress from This World, to That Which Is to Come (1678) by John Bunyan is an allegory regarded as one of the most significant works of English literature. Told by a dreamer, Pilgrim’s Progress follows the travels of a man, Christian, through a series of allegorical places: the Slough of Despond, the House Beautiful, the Valley of Humiliation, the Valley of the Shadow of Death, Vanity Fair, Doubting Castle, and so on, to the Celestial City that he seeks. Valiant-for-Truth is a strong, sword-wielding pilgrim who drives off three attackers single-handedly and joins Christian’s group at the end of its journey.约翰·班扬（John Bunyan）的《天路历程：从这个世界到将来要承受的世界》（The Pilgrim's Progress from This World, to That Which Is to Come，1678 年）是一部寓言，被视为英国文学最重要的作品之一。由一个梦者讲述，《天路历程》跟随一个名叫“基督徒”（Christian）的男子走过一系列寓言般的地方：绝望潭、美丽宫、屈辱谷、死荫谷、名利场、疑堡等等，最终抵达他所寻求的天上城。“勇士”（Valiant-for-Truth）是一个强壮、持剑的朝圣者，他单枪匹马击退三名袭击者，在旅程末尾加入了基督徒的队伍。 “My sword I leave to him who can wield it.”

嗯，一次毕业典礼上讲这些，已经足够。我希望一个老人的这些沉思对你们有用。最后，我所说的话，指向的是《天路历程429Pilgrim’s ProgressThe Pilgrim’s Progress from This World, to That Which Is to Come (1678) by John Bunyan is an allegory regarded as one of the most significant works of English literature. Told by a dreamer, Pilgrim’s Progress follows the travels of a man, Christian, through a series of allegorical places: the Slough of Despond, the House Beautiful, the Valley of Humiliation, the Valley of the Shadow of Death, Vanity Fair, Doubting Castle, and so on, to the Celestial City that he seeks. Valiant-for-Truth is a strong, sword-wielding pilgrim who drives off three attackers single-handedly and joins Christian’s group at the end of its journey.约翰·班扬（John Bunyan）的《天路历程：从这个世界到将来要承受的世界》（The Pilgrim's Progress from This World, to That Which Is to Come，1678 年）是一部寓言，被视为英国文学最重要的作品之一。由一个梦者讲述，《天路历程》跟随一个名叫“基督徒”（Christian）的男子走过一系列寓言般的地方：绝望潭、美丽宫、屈辱谷、死荫谷、名利场、疑堡等等，最终抵达他所寻求的天上城。“勇士”（Valiant-for-Truth）是一个强壮、持剑的朝圣者，他单枪匹马击退三名袭击者，在旅程末尾加入了基督徒的队伍。》（Pilgrim's Progress）中老“真理剑客”（Valiant-for-Truth）唯一可能的结局：“我的剑，留给能挥舞它的人。”
